name: potato
soil: Loose, well-drained sandy loam rich in organic matter, pH 5.5–7.0

stages.name: Planting / Sprouting
stages.description: Seed tubers are planted on ridges; sprouts come up in 2–3 weeks.
stages.irrigation: First light irrigation within 2–3 days of planting (or plant in moist soil). Water should reach only two-thirds up the ridge.
stages.fertilizer: Basal at planting: 8–10 tonnes FYM + 75 kg DAP + 70 kg MOP + 55 kg urea per acre.
watch_for: Seed tubers rotting in wet soil
Cutworms cutting young shoots at night
tips: Use healthy, sprouted seed tubers of 30–50 g — about 10–12 quintals per acre
Rows 60 cm apart, tubers 20 cm apart

stages.name: Vegetative Growth
stages.description: Stems and leaves grow; stolons start forming underground.
stages.irrigation: Every 8–10 days; keep the ridges moist but never flooded.
stages.fertilizer: Second dose: 55 kg urea per acre at 25–30 days, then earth up.
tips: Earth up at 25–30 days to cover the tubers and stop greening
In cool, foggy weather start a preventive Mancozeb 2.5 g/litre spray

stages.name: Tuber Initiation
stages.description: Stolon tips swell into small tubers. Water stress now means fewer tubers.
stages.irrigation: Every 7–8 days — the most critical time for water.
watch_for: Late blight — dark water-soaked patches on leaves with white mould underneath, spreading fast in cold, humid weather
tips: At the first sign of late blight spray Cymoxanil + Mancozeb 3 g/litre or Metalaxyl + Mancozeb 2.5 g/litre
A light irrigation protects the crop on frosty nights

stages.name: Tuber Bulking
stages.description: Tubers grow fast and gain weight.
stages.irrigation: Every 7–10 days; even moisture prevents cracked and hollow tubers.
tips: Repeat blight sprays every 7–10 days while foggy, humid weather lasts

stages.name: Maturity / Harvest
stages.description: Leaves yellow, vines dry and the tuber skin sets.
stages.irrigation: Stop irrigation 10 days before cutting the vines.
watch_for: Tubers cut or bruised while digging
tips: Cut the vines (haulms) 10–15 days before digging so the skin hardens
Cure tubers in shade for 10–15 days before storage

common_pests.name: Aphids
common_pests.symptoms: Tiny green insects under leaves; they spread viruses in seed crops
common_pests.control: Thiamethoxam 25 WG 0.2 g/litre; cut the vines early in a seed crop

common_pests.name: Cutworm
common_pests.symptoms: Young shoots cut at ground level at night
common_pests.control: Chlorpyriphos 20 EC 2 ml/litre sprayed on the ridges in the evening

common_pests.name: Potato tuber moth
common_pests.symptoms: Tunnels in tubers in the field and in storage
common_pests.control: Earth up well so no tuber is exposed; store in a cool place and cover stored tubers with dry neem leaves

common_diseases.name: Late blight
common_diseases.symptoms: Dark water-soaked patches on leaves with white mould underneath; the whole field can collapse in days
common_diseases.control: Mancozeb 2.5 g/litre before it appears; Cymoxanil + Mancozeb 3 g/litre or Metalaxyl + Mancozeb 2.5 g/litre once seen

common_diseases.name: Early blight
common_diseases.symptoms: Brown spots with rings (like a target) on older leaves

common_diseases.name: Black scurf
common_diseases.symptoms: Black crusts on the tuber skin, weak sprouting
common_diseases.control: Dip seed tubers in 3% boric acid for 20–30 minutes before storage or planting
